correctness.rationale: After restricting to the end-time prefix, upper triangularity preserves invertibility of the change of basis. In the rows born after s, each surviving nonzero reduced column still has its distinct last nonzero row, so any zero linear combination has zero coefficients on all surviving columns. This gives exactly the eligible-column kernel basis, including zero reduced columns at s=0 and tied births. For fixed t the eligible sets are nested; orthogonal remainders are nonzero by independence. The projection onto the chain space is the sum of ww^T/(w^T w), so the boundary on both sides gives the stated rank-one update including the correct induced metric and zero padding. As a direct exact check, start with two vertices a,b, then add c and the two edges ac,bc simultaneously. At the earlier start the kernel of the c-row [1,1] is generated by (1,-1), yielding the matrix (1/2)[[1,-1],[-1,1]]. Including c at the start gives the ordinary three-vertex path Laplacian; a subsequently born isolated vertex with no new edge appends a zero row and column. All k_t insertions cost O(m k_t^2+(nm+n^2)k_t) including dense updates. There are at most k_t dense event snapshots per row and O(n^2) initialization per row. The final k_t=m row absorbs O((n+m)m^2) reduction, and input/output handling on the specified event grid does not exceed the bound. The uploaded checker was inspected, not run: its event path compares sweep entries with rational nullspace projection, while its extra checks use the eligible basis directly at birth-index pairs rather than testing the retrieval of stored snapshots, and do not literally visit every integer time when a level is empty. These limits do not affect the proof.

evidence: Mémoli–Wan–Wang sweep in decreasing s by Schur complements at fixed t; they give O(t(n_q^t)^2+n_{q+1}^t) for the stated single-simplex filtration, without persistence-basis orthogonalization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: This covers all-pairs matrix assembly in its setting and can be cheaper. One can also refine tied levels and eliminate only rows incident to active upper simplices, yielding at most (q+2)k_t such rows at fixed q, with zero padding handled separately. Such Schur bounds do not analyze the particular reduced-column method. The record has value as a guarantee for that method, not as a new best general upper bound on the problem.

evidence: Prior per-update costs already control adding vectors to a selected predecessor. The paper leaves the global bound as future work. A same-row policy guarantees nothing gets inserted twice within a row; an arbitrary predecessor policy does not give that accounting.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The record realizes a concrete version of the conjectural order via a simple additional scheduling and amortization argument; it does not settle the behavior of the unrestricted earlier implementation.

value.rationale: The specific reuse guarantee makes dense matrix assembly costs predictable for workflows that already have persistence columns; tied versus staggered end levels can change the assembly bound by a factor of m. This is modest but useful and answers an explicit method-specific complexity question. It does not promise numerical stability, eigensolver costs, faster Schur assembly, or optimality.
